summary: Bibb County steel lookout tower: site chosen July 1926, reported completed April 1927 on donated land; site location conflicts; no later record found.

events.note: Reported completed in April 1927, described as the third tower the state had erected. Site chosen July 1926. The two reports give different locations.
Site donated to the state by the Kaul Land and Lumber Company.

evidence.supports: July 10, 1926 (Birmingham Post-Herald): Bunker, state forester, selected a Bibb County site
evidence.quote: Col. Page S. Bunker, state forester, returned today from Bibb county where he selected a site for a lookout tower

evidence.supports: Post-Herald report: site at a point six to seven miles east of Centerville
evidence.quote: at a point six to seven miles east of Centerville.

evidence.supports: April 27, 1927 (Birmingham News): steel tower completed in Bibb County, third built by the state
evidence.quote: A steel lookout tower, the third to be erected by the state, has been completed in Bibb County

evidence.supports: Birmingham News: site about seven miles west of Randolph
evidence.quote: The site chosen is in the southeaster part of the county, about seven miles west of Randolph.

evidence.supports: Kaul Land and Lumber Company donated the site to the state
evidence.quote: The tract belongs to the Kaul Land and Lumber Company which, when advised of the project, promptly donated the site to the state.

evidence.supports: Birmingham News reports the State Commission of Forestry felt Bibb County was entitled to precedence for the first 1927 tower
evidence.quote: the State Commission of Forestry felt that this county was entitled to precedence in the erection of the first lookout tower to be built in 1927

evidence.supports: NHLR Bibb Lookout Tower (a different registered tower) was built in 1949
evidence.quote: Bibbs Fire Tower was built in 1949.

notes_for_editor: Location conflict is unresolved: the 1926 Birmingham Post-Herald report says six to seven miles east of Centerville; the 1927 Birmingham News report says about seven miles west of Randolph in the southeastern part of the county. Needs a second source or a field check before the coordinates are trusted. The Maud name is the Forest Lookouts page's own label for both reports; no other source found ties it to this tower. The NHLR Bibb Lookout Tower (US 809, AL 10) is dated 1949, after the April 1927 tower, so it is probably a different structure and should not be merged. Its coordinates are not compared with the Maud entry point, because no source gives coordinates for that point. No height is given in any source. Nothing after 1927 was found, so status, staffing and today's site are unknown. A video title in search results mentions a forgotten fire tower in Bibb County; it was not read and is not cited.
